caption: : Avg. performance across 11 datasets (y-axis) consistently improves as the number of training examples increases (x-axis). Max is 29k examples, the full size of our dataset.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of training dataset examples and average performance. The x-axis is labeled "# of training dataset (k)" and features a linear scale with a visible range extending slightly below 5 to slightly above 30, displaying numeric tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis is labeled "Avgerage Performance" and utilizes a linear scale with a visible range extending from just below 48 to slightly above 56, featuring numeric tick marks at intervals of 2. The data is represented by a single solid black line with circular markers. The line exhibits a steady, continuous upward trend as the x-axis values increase. It begins at an x-axis value of 5 with a y-axis value of approximately 47.5, increases to roughly 50.3 at an x-axis value of 10, reaches approximately 52.6 at an x-axis value of 20, and ends at its maximum y-axis value of approximately 56.2 at an x-axis value of 29.
